messages:
maria: Heads-up — prod p99 for short seq (<=32) generation doubled starting ~02:15 UTC after last runtime canary. Traces point at a kernel path change, not obvious load increase.
josh: I saw that alert too, dashboards show throughput steady, CPU/gpu util ok but p99 jumps on a subset of pods. Any recent Triton/driver flips?
maria: Canary notes: triton runtime 2.12.7 rolled with kernel-selector optimizer enabled + driver 535.86 on canary pool. deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-15T02:10Z triton-2.12.7->stable canary.
sam: grabbing perf counters from one affected pod now. nv-nsight shows SM_efficiency drop and L2 reads way up during token emission for 8-16 token inputs. Posting snippet: ```ncu --metrics sm_efficiency,l2_hit_rate,dram_read_throughput --target-processes all
==> sm_efficiency 54% | l2_hit_rate 26% | dram_bw 820GB/s```
lina: interesting — our FlashAttention kernel usually keeps sm_eff >85% for these short seqs. Looks like it fell back to a different attention path (cuBLAS/implicit GEMM).
josh: Could be selector heuristic now picking a general GEMM for small workspace estimates. That would also change memory access patterns and could cause KV cache eviction patterns to shift.
maria: Logs show triton selector reason: ``selected_kernel=implicit_gemm workspace=45MB est_perf=0.74`` where previously it chose ``flash_kernel workspace=60MB est_perf=0.92`` for same model/batch.
sam: Also seeing increased KV cache churn: eviction spikes align with p99 spikes. Possibly different kernel memory alignment causing buffer re-allocs and KV cache fragmentation.
lina: Reproduced on canary VM: forcing FLASH kernel via env override returns p99 to baseline. Command used: ```export TRITON_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=flash_attention; ./run_infer ...```
josh: Good repro. Nearby note: driver 535.86 includes a new cuBLAS heuristic that changed workspace estimation for grouped GEMMs — might influence Triton's selector.
maria: Immediate mitigation: 1) pin selector to prefer flash kernel for models with seq<=64 via runtime flag 2) roll back triton canary to 2.12.6 on affected pool 3) add perf-test to CI for short-seq kernel selection. Who can take which?
sam: I can push the runtime flag hotfix and a canary rollback now. Pushing patch branch: `hotfix/force-flash-shortseq` and starting rollout to canary.
josh: I'll add a regression test to the perf suite that asserts kernel choice for short seqs and records nvprof numbers. PR incoming.
lina: I'll open an upstream issue with Triton linking our selector logs and driver version. Might be accepted as selector-change bug.
maria: Ops: Sam, after hotfix can we run a 1h canary then promote? Also capture a full kv-cache heap snapshot before/after.
sam: Yes. Starting canary hotfix now. deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-15T02:45Z hotfix/force-flash-shortseq -> canary.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01 | p99 spike short-seq attention kernel regression. Severity: P2.
maria: Postmortem actions (short): - roll triton back if hotfix unstable - add kernel-selection telemetry to traces - ensure driver bump checklist includes kernel-selector smoke for short-seq models - schedule postmortem doc. Assign: sam (hotfix+rollback), josh (regressions+CI), lina (Triton issue), maria (postmortem).
josh: Quick note: also add an automated canary metric to fail a deploy if flash kernel share drops below 85% for short-seq traffic.
maria: Thanks. I'll update the incident board and link perf artifacts: nvprof traces, triton selector logs, kv-heap dumps in the incident ticket.
